rules.source: Privacy Act 1988 (Commonwealth), 13 Australian Privacy Principles (APPs); a dedicated Children's Online Privacy Code is required to be developed by the OAIC by 10 December 2026. Official: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC), https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-registers/privacy-codes/childrens-online-privacy-code
rules.retrieved_snippet: The Commonwealth Privacy Act 1988 provides protection for personal information based on 13 principles (the Australian Privacy Principles, or APPs)... The Amendment Act requires the OAIC to develop the Code to address online privacy for children by 10 December 2026.

rules.source: Online Safety Act 2021, enforced by the eSafety Commissioner; includes the Social Media Minimum Age scheme and Unlawful and Age-restricted material Codes. Official: OAIC, https://www.oaic.gov.au/news/blog/a-safer-internet-doesnt-need-to-compromise-privacy
rules.retrieved_snippet: In Australia, the Privacy Act 1988 and Online Safety Act 2021 play distinct and essential roles in protecting children online... including the introduction of the Social Media Minimum Age scheme, the completed Online Safety Act 2021 review and the Unlawful and Age-restricted material Codes registered by the eSafety Commissioner.

rules.source: Australian Consumer Law (Schedule 2 of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010), enforced by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) under a one-law/multiple-regulators system with state/territory regulators. Official: https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/buying-products-and-services/consumer-rights-and-guarantees
rules.retrieved_snippet: The Australian Consumer Law is written into Schedule 2 of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010... Under the Australian Consumer Law, businesses must meet a set of basic rights called consumer guarantees when they sell products or services.
